title: Landing Conductor: artifact fingerprint capture and staged compatibility sweeper
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Implement an end-to-end 'Landing Conductor' that automates fingerprinting, provenance capture, deterministic format harmonization, conversion to runtime artifacts, and a staged compatibility sweeper (micro-canary) for newly submitted open-source LLM weights. The conductor unifies intake sources (HF, OSS manifests, partner FTP) into a single canonical artifact record, emits a signed provenance bundle, and triggers downstream conversion + smoke validation.

Why now: Our current onboarding flow is manual and brittle for heterogeneous weight formats, leading to flaky canaries, missed runtime incompatibilities, and long lead times to publish a performance profile and pinned version. This project reduces manual triage, improves deterministic validations, and shortens time-to-publish for new models while preserving safety checks and auditability.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical artifact record is created for every new intake event with stable fingerprint fields: sha256(weights), manifest_hash, format_type, source_uri, and claim_signature
Automated conversion pipeline can consume the canonical record to produce runtime artifacts (runtime .bin, quantized variants) with deterministic outputs given same inputs

A staged compatibility sweeper runs a micro-canary that replays a standard smoke prompt set and validates P95 latency and token-per-second against the baseline; failures create a pinned 'incompatible' flag and stop profile publishing
Performance profile (latency distribution, memory footprint, tokens/sec) is published to the model catalog for release runtime-1.24 when all checks pass
Audit log and provenance bundle (linkable) are persisted and accessible via the Console UI for compliance reviews
End-to-end pipeline runs (from intake -> profile publish) complete within SLA 24 hours for small models (<10B) and provide telemetry for larger models
implementation_notes: Intake adapters: extend existing HF ingesters to populate canonical_artifact record and upload original manifest to artifact-store
Fingerprinting: compute sha256 of full weight tarball + canonicalize JSON manifest then compute manifest_hash; store both in artifact_fingerprints table
Provenance bundle: bundle original manifest, conversion logs, env image hash, and GPG-like claim signature (initially HMAC using internal key)
Conversion step: invoke converter service (converter-v2) to produce runtime-friendly artifacts and create deterministic metadata; surface conversion warnings in artifact record

Compatibility sweeper: implement a lightweight runner that replays 25 deterministic prompts (shared smoke set) against quantized and fp16 variants; compare latency P50/P95 to profile baseline and check tokenization parity

Profile publisher: after sweeper pass, synthesize profile JSON and call catalog-publish endpoint with pin recommendation heuristics (prefer quantized-8bit variant if throughput delta < 15% and hallucination checks pass)
Observability: emit spans for each stage, per-artifact metrics (conversion_duration_ms, canary_pass, p95_latency_ms), and an end-to-end trace ID for debugging
Database migrations: add artifact_fingerprints table with columns (key, sha256, manifest_hash, format, source, created_by, created_at)
tasks: Design canonical_artifact schema and add DB migration
HF/OSS intake adapter change to produce canonical records
Implement fingerprinting library and artifact_fingerprints table population
Wire converter-v2 to consume canonical records and emit deterministic metadata
Build micro-canary runner and integrate with sweeper orchestration
Profile synthesis and catalog publish logic
Console: add link to provenance bundle and per-artifact timeline
E2E tests and performance benchmarking on small/medium models
Security review and HMAC key rotation policy for claim signatures
risks: Format explosion: new archive/weight layouts may require frequent adapter updates; mitigate by extensible parser registry
False negatives in canary due to env differences; mitigate with pinned runtime images and synthetic baseline builds
Sensitive weight exposure: ensure original weight blobs are stored with limited access in artifact-store and accompanied by KMS-encrypted metadata
Long-running conversions for very large models may exceed orchestration timeouts; plan for chunked conversion and streaming progress reports
open_questions: Do we require an external notarization (third-party signature) for high-risk community models?
What is the canonical smoke prompt set scope — should it include multilingual samples and instruction-following cases?
Should pin recommendation be auto-applied for low-risk models or require PM approval?
Who will own the HMAC key and rotation cadence for claim signatures? Security or Platform?
